# MDL011 mdl-module

A `part of` name differs from the root `module`, two roots share a module name, or an included file declares `module`.

## What it does

One model has exactly one `module` declaration, in its root file.

## Why it matters

A model is one namespace. Two module names, or a part that claims another module, splits the references that were meant to meet.

## Remedy

Declare `module` once, in the root file, and write `part of <that module>` everywhere else.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb config="included"
grimble = "2";
part of other;
node a : trusted {
}
```

### Clean case 2

```grmb expect=clean file=design/model.grmb config="included"
grimble = "2";
part of m;
node a : trusted {
}
```

## Examples

### MDL011 one module per model / A part of another module fires #1 (line 6) (fire)

```text
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "a.grmb";
=== design/a.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of other;
```

### MDL011 one module per model / A part of the root module is clean #2 (line 17) (clean)

```text
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "a.grmb";
=== design/a.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
```
